CORRECTION: This test was designed to confirm the 'narrow locus at layers 20-23' hypothesis by removing exactly those layers from an otherwise-full ablation and checking whether the IFE DEF collapse disappears. It did NOT disappear (IFE_def=0.0, full collapse, same as every other sufficiently-broad ablation tested). This means layers 20-23 are NOT uniquely necessary for the effect -- the earlier 'precise mechanistic localization' framing was wrong. CORRECTED interpretation, synthesizing all layer-sweep data points: (a) 4 layers alone (20-23) -> collapse; (b) 5 layers alone (24-28) -> NO collapse; (c) 21 layers excluding 20-23 -> collapse. This pattern is consistent with a BREADTH/DOSE THRESHOLD effect (ablating 'enough' layers in aggregate triggers the collapse, with some layer-position sensitivity affecting exactly where the threshold sits) rather than a specific narrow causal locus. The 24-28-alone result being just below threshold and 20-23-alone being just above it does not mean 20-23 is special -- it means both were independently sufficient/insufficient at the margin, and larger ablations (21 layers) are comfortably above threshold regardless of which specific layers are included. Retracting the 'targeted fix: avoid layers 20-23' next-step proposed in the previous commit -- this exclusion test directly falsifies it. This is exactly the kind of hypothesis-correction the random-control statistical work modeled: propose a precise mechanistic claim, test it directly, report the correction openly when the test fails it.
